summary: Added the console's standard position component and a playable game with an in-browser solver. web/components/Drop7Board.tsx renders one Drop7 position with optional incoming disc, highlighted/dimmed cells, drop marker and a per-column readout, so theory and concept pages can show the decision a policy faces; web/components/discs.tsx holds the disc palette and the DOM (DiscFace) and SVG (CellGlyph) disc renderers ported from the author's blog simulator, and Board.tsx's Board/BoardCompare/Disc shorthands now render through them. web/components/Drop7Game.tsx is the simulator (play / evaluate / auto modes, engine animation frames, reproducible seeds, browser-local personal best) mounted at /play and registered for MDX. The solver is web/lib/play/fast-search.ts: the reference evaluateMoves from src/core/typescript/solver.ts with the board-state optimisations of finding-13 ported to TypeScript (mask-based popper detection with 128-entry run tables, in-place gravity on touched columns, wave counting instead of wave lists, an allocation-free leaf in fast-leaf.ts, and a packed seven-word key in a typed-array LRU transposition table in fast-cache.ts). Parity tests (web/lib/play/*.test.ts) assert identical outcome streams and probabilities, bit-identical leaf utilities for every profile, and identical column values, best column, work, node and cache counts against the reference on positions reached through play, including aborted and depth-4 searches. Profiling showed the reference's string-keyed Map was ~85% of a JS decision; the packed-key table is where the speedup comes from. next.config.ts widens Turbopack's root to the repository so web/ imports src/ directly.
validationPerformed: cd web && npm test: 14 of 14 parity tests pass (fast-cache equivalence vs Map LRU under random traffic; leaf bit-identical for all 5 profiles on >700 root boards and >5,000 chance outcomes; outcome streams identical on >20,000 outcomes incl. budget aborts; depth-2/3/4 and work-limited searches deepEqual to evaluateMoves minus elapsedMs)

Informational timing in the suite, interleaved reference/fast on the same depth-3 decisions, this non-exclusive workstation: reference 8.9 s vs fast 1.7 s (5.4x); earlier probe over 17 decisions: 5.5x at depth 2, 5.7x at depth 3. Not a benchmark profile.

cd web && npx tsc --noEmit clean; eslint clean on changed files; next build passes; web/scripts/check-routes.sh against the dev server: 144 routes, 0 non-200; /play exercised in Chromium in play, evaluate and auto modes; BoardCompare and rules figures inspected
limitations: Self-reported contribution; not yet independently reviewed.
